candidates.title: DAYJOB: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Professional Work
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026 AABA4ET Workshop (per arXiv comments field; workshop, not main track)
candidates.institution: Not stated in paper; GitHub org 'surge-ai' and a self-cited blog post suggest a possible Surge AI link, unconfirmed
communitySignals: Not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code within this round's research scope
credibilityEvidence: arxiv.org/html/2610.01306v1 §3.5: task construction by named domain professionals, three-layer review
Table 2: median 47.5/57.5 binary rubric criteria per task
§4.3: grading done by an agentic LLM judge (OpenCode + Claude Opus 4.8), never validated against human expert agreement
Table 3/§5.1: main results table confirmed matching abstract exactly
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Core low-pass-rate finding is robust across grading thresholds (§5.2, relaxed τ=0.90 gives 62.4%/58.3%), but the grading judge's own validity against human experts is never measured, and the 'human-equivalent hours' figure (Table 2 footnotes) is a task-creator self-estimate, not a measured human baseline
reproducibilityEvidence: 50/80 finance tasks public, 30 withheld on request
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Directional claim (long professional tasks remain very hard for agents) is well supported; precise percentages depend on an unvalidated LLM judge, so exact numbers should be read with appropriate caution
candidates.primaryLimitation: The agentic grading judge was never validated against human expert graders; no dedicated Limitations section exists in the paper
candidates.presentationReason: Method, rubric construction, and results are clearly laid out across sections; the absence of judge-validation and human-baseline discussion is a content gap, not a clarity gap
candidates.reason: Selected as the clearest, most concrete demonstration of a real capability gap on professional long-horizon work; forms the 'evaluation reveals a limit' anchor of today's evaluation-reliability cluster alongside 2610.00651 and 2610.02206

candidates.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track (confirmed directly from arXiv Comments metadata field)
candidates.institution: Not stated in paper; GitHub org 'RISys-Lab'
credibilityEvidence: Appendix A: human-in-the-loop verification is author-only, no external annotators or IAA figure
Table 1: best open-weight model (GLM-5.2, 753B) at 41.3% Exact Correct unrestricted, confirming the <42% ceiling
Appendix G.2/§4.1: RedSage-K (8B SFT+GRPO) at 79.2% Avg Total Score vs DeepSeek-V3.2 (685B MoE) at 80.2% -- the actual basis of the 'parity' claim
Table 1: Hinted-mode Exact Correct shows RedSage-K at 69.4% vs DeepSeek-V3.2 at 84.5% -- a 15pp gap not surfaced by the aggregate parity framing
arxiv.org/abs/2610.02206 Comments field: 'Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track' confirmed directly from arXiv metadata
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Large-scale (8,504 pairs, 1,642 tools, 24 open-weight configs + proprietary comparisons, 3 query modes) and peer-reviewed at a dedicated NeurIPS track; the 'parity' claim is real but mode-dependent, not uniform
reproducibilityEvidence: Dataset+pipeline code on GitHub (RISys-Lab/KaliBench, CC BY-NC 4.0)
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Peer-reviewed venue, large scale, and numbers trace cleanly to body tables even after accounting for the mode-dependent nuance in the parity claim
candidates.primaryLimitation: The '8B matches 685B' claim holds only on the aggregate average score; a 15-percentage-point gap remains on exact-command accuracy in Hinted mode, and human verification was author-only rather than independently annotated
candidates.presentationReason: Dataset construction, training setup, and results tables are explicit and well-organized across the main text and appendices
candidates.reason: Selected as the methods/fix counterpart to today's cluster -- shows a concrete, reproducible training recipe (RLVR) that closes most of a capability gap, balancing the gloomier findings of 2610.01306 and 2610.00651
